nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiFe LDH synthesis
nodes.procedure: nickel(II) nitrate hexahydrate Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and iron(II) sulfate heptahydrate FeSO4·7H2O in a specific molar ratio were dissolved in 35 mL deionized water, followed by the addition of 300 mg urea and 120 mg ammonium fluoride. After stirring for 30 min, the suspension was transferred to a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and heated at 120 °C for 10 h before cooling to room temperature. The resultant precipitate was centrifuged and washed with deionized water and ethanol and dried at 60 °C for 1 h. The doping level of Fe atoms in the host structure of Ni hydroxide was controlled by precisely regulating the molar ratio of Ni/Fe salts in the precursor solution, while with the same total amount of metal ions in the initial solutions (Ni2+ + Fe2+ = 1 mmol).
nodes.source_text: Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and FeSO4·7H2O... dried at 60 °C for 1 h. The doping level... (Ni2+ + Fe2+ = 1 mmol).

nodes.name: Sulfidation to Ni1-xFexS2
nodes.procedure: The as-prepared NiFeOxHy LDH was sufficiently mixed with sulphur powder (Alfa Aesar, ~100 mesh, 99.5%, 1:5) by grinding for 30 min. The mixture was then placed in the center of a quartz tube in an aluminum oxide boat, and heated at 400 °C for 1 h in an argon atmosphere to obtain pyrite Ni1-xFexS2. Finally, the obtained compounds were ultrasonicated, washed several times and dried under vacuum overnight.
nodes.source_text: The as-prepared NiFeOxHy LDH was sufficiently mixed with sulphur powder (1:5)... dried under vacuum overnight.

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder XRD patterns of Ni_{1-x}Fe_x S_2 match standard cubic pyrite-type NiS₂ (JCPDS No. 65-3325) with diffraction peak shift to higher angle with increasing Fe substitution due to lattice contraction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in Fig. 2a, the diffraction peaks of the as-prepared Ni_{1-x}Fe_x S_2 match with those of standard cubic (Pa-3) pyrite-type materials (JCPDS No. 65-3325).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals nanosheet morphology of Ni_{0.8}Fe_{0.2}S_2 with uniform thickness distribution between 10-20 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In scanning electron microscopy (SEM) ... close-up inspection of Ni_{0.8}Fe_{0.2}S_2 NSs reveals nanosheet structures whose thickness uniformly distributes between 10 and 20 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows nanosheet morphology and HRTEM displays lattice fringes with 2.49 Å spacing indexed to (210) plane of Ni_{0.8}Fe_{0.2}S_2 with single-crystal-like diffraction pattern.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image (Fig. 2d) displays clear lattice fringes with an interplanar spacing of 2.49 Å, indexed to the (210) plane of Ni_{0.8}Fe_{0.2}S_2 NSs.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mappings confirm uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, and S elements throughout Ni_{0.8}Fe_{0.2}S_2 nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive X-ray spectrum (EDS) elemental mappings of Ni_{0.8}Fe_{0.2}S_2 NSs provide direct-viewing evidence for the uniform distribution of Ni, Fe and S elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows absorption edge shift to lower energy with increasing Fe substitution, indicating decreased Ni valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) results present the Ni absorption-edge shifts to the lower-energy side as the substituted Fe concentration increases.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT Ni K-edge EXAFS shows Ni-S peak at ~1.9 Å and Ni-Ni at 3.5 Å; Fe substitution weakens Ni-S first shell, indicating lower coordination number and more sulfur vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Two separate peaks (peaks I and II) at ~1.9 and 3.5 Å are assigned to the features of Ni–S and Ni–Ni bonds ... the first-shell peak I is weakened by Fe substitution.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ electrochemical Raman spectroscopy during HER shows characteristic NiS₂ peaks decay and Ni₃S₂ peaks emerge/grow for Ni_{1-x}Fe_x S_2 as potential decreases from 0.4 to -0.25 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the Raman peaks of pristine pyrite-type NiS₂ and heazlewoodite-type Ni₃S₂ from Fig. S7 ... the characteristic peaks in Fig. 3a have been identified.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p3/2 XPS peaks shift to lower binding energies in Ni_{1-x}Fe_x S_2 with Fe substitution, consistent with decreased Ni valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nominal Ni valence states are supported by the K-edge absorption positions ... which are in line with the facts of Ni 2p3/2 X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) peaks shifting to lower binding energies in Ni_{1-x}Fe_x S_2.
